title: The Hold Point
brief: On a Meridian Build site, the foreman wants to place the ground floor slab at 7 a.m. tomorrow; the concrete is booked. The reinforcement inspection hold point (H-6) has not been signed because the client's engineer cannot attend until noon. The foreman proposes pouring and "getting it signed after". Site safety and legal requirements are managed separately and are outside this visit. You have 12 visit points to decide.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

evidence.text: ITP hold point H-6 requires the client's engineer to sign before concrete is placed.
Hold point sheet H-6 shows "pour approved" pencilled by the foreman with no engineer signature.
evidence.whyItMatters: A hold point may only be released by the named authority.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check who signed the hold point.

evidence.text: Foreman: "We always get it signed after. The engineer never finds anything." (note 1)
evidence.whyItMatters: Supervisors must support planned controls; past results do not justify bypassing a hold point.

evidence.text: Foreman confirms only the client's engineer can release H-6.
Contract clause 31 allows the client to require removal of work covered before a hold point is released.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read contract terms on hold points.

evidence.text: Supplier: "We can move the booking to 1 p.m. at no cost if told by 4 p.m. today."
Internal reinforcement check IR-6 found 2 laps short; corrected and re-checked this afternoon.
evidence.whyItMatters: Internal checks find issues; the engineer's inspection remains required.

evidence.text: Project manager: "A half-day delay costs less than breaking out a slab." Estimate E-12 confirms this.
Concrete order confirms the specified mix and quantity.
Programme poster shows the pour date in red.
Bar spacers are of an approved type.

options: Move the pour to 1 p.m., ask the engineer to inspect at noon, and erase the pencilled approval
decisions.rationale: A short delay meets the hold point at no cost.
optionFeedback: Covers work before a required inspection.
Meets the requirement with minimal impact.

decisions.prompt: How do you respond to "we always get it signed after"?
options: Explain calmly that the hold point protects the work and the client's right to inspect, and show that the 1 p.m. option keeps the programme
decisions.rationale: Address the habit with facts and a practical route.

containment: Do not pour until H-6 is signed; remove the pencilled approval
correction: Rebook the pour for after the engineer's inspection
cause: Hold points can be marked approved by anyone, and pours are booked before inspection times are confirmed
corrective: Allow only the named authority to sign hold points and book pours only after inspection is scheduled
effectiveness: Audit hold point sheets against pour dates monthly

debriefText.found: You protected the hold point without losing the day.
debriefText.missed: Ask suppliers about flexibility before accepting a deadline.
debriefText.falseFinding: Posters and approved spacers are not findings.
